text:
marta: FYI onboarding customer hit a weird parity bug between Java SDK and REST around structured outputs + streaming. REST supports response_format=structured which returns JSON objects per chunk; Java SDK only gives raw strings and loses the function_call wrapper.

ryan: can you paste the REST curl that worked and the Java snippet that failed?

marta: REST curl that worked (server sends streaming json chunks):
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-structured-1","prompt":"summarize","response_format":"structured","stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

marta: Java SDK call we used (redwood-java v0.3.0):
```java
RedwoodClient client = new RedwoodClient(System.getenv("REDWOOD_KEY"));
client.generateStream(new GenerateRequest.Builder()
  .model("gpt-structured-1")
  .prompt("summarize")
  .stream(true)
  .build(), event -> {
    System.out.println(event.getText()); // prints plain text only
  });
```

marta: result: SDK prints chunked text but missing the function call metadata: {"type":"function_call","name":"extract_entities","arguments":{...}} -> we only see the arguments string inlined, not the wrapper, so sample app can't route to tool.

indra: thanks. two possible things: (1) param name drift: REST uses response_format whereas SDK uses responseFormat and we didn't wire the structured mode through; (2) streaming parser in Java SDK assumes simple text-event lines and strips JSON wrappers.

ryan: I also noticed Java SDK default temperature was 0.8 in client ctor but REST default is 0.0 for generation. That caused different output content and made structured parsing fail intermittently. So three things: param mapping, streaming JSON wrapper handling, and default param drift.

ci-bot: failing test redwood-java/tests/integration/stream_structured_test.java on main.

marta: temporary workaround for customer: call REST directly and parse SSE chunks manually (ugly). We added a small helper in sample-java: https://github.com/redwood/sample-java-onboard/pull/14 which hits REST endpoint with response_format=structured.

indra: plan: (A) update Java SDK to accept responseFormat and map it to response_format when building request, (B) update streaming parser to detect JSON-wrapped events and pass the full JSON event (including function_call) to the callback instead of only text, (C) align default generation params to REST (temperature=0.0) or document differences clearly. I'll open PRs.

ryan: please add a test that streams a function_call event and asserts we receive the wrapper with type=="function_call" and name set. Also add test to assert default temperature parity.

indra: will do. Also adding a small integration that runs sample-java against staging to ensure tool routing in sample app works.

ci-bot: created issues RNF-2628 (java streaming parse), RNF-2629 (param mapping responseFormat), RNF-2630 (default param parity).

marta: timeline? customer demo tomorrow morning.

indra: I'll try to get a small hotfix release v0.3.1 that includes streaming parse fix and responseFormat alias. If we can't ship in time, sample-java will include the REST helper and docs.

ryan: QA checklist: reproduce with staged endpoint, assert function_call events are delivered intact, verify no behavior regressions for non-streaming users.

marta: confirmed REST helper works and demo is unblocked for now. leaving reproduction steps in sample issue: https://github.com/redwood/sample-java-onboard/issues/7

indra: opened PRs and added unit+integration tests; requesting patch release.

devx-bot: release note draft: "Fix: Java SDK: streaming parser preserves structured events (function_call) and supports responseFormat mapping; align default generation params with REST." scheduled for v0.3.1. :rocket:

marta: thanks all, please add a short note in SDK migration docs about responseFormat vs response_format and streaming behavior.

devx-bot: thread archived.
